transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I guess what brings me in is... well, I don't want to sound like I'm complaining, because I know people have it much worse. But recently, the things that usually make me feel like myself have just started feeling... I don't know, kind of flat? And heavy. 

Like, I usually love my weekend photography walks, and mentoring the kids, and even just keeping a really clean, organized calendar for work—I'm an executive assistant, so I usually pride myself on being very on top of things. But lately, I've just sort of stopped initiating any of it. I feel a little embarrassed even admitting that out loud, honestly, because it's just not like me to drop the ball. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, let me think... I guess it's been a little while now. Maybe about a year and three months? I probably should have come in sooner, I'm sorry. I just kept hoping I could push through it, you know? 

It sort of started after... well, a family member of mine had some changes in their health, and their behavior changed a bit, too. So I stepped in and took on a lot more of the coordination and planning for them. Which I really don't mind at all! I'm happy to be there for my family. But I think that's around the time things started feeling a bit heavier for me. 

Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I hope that's helpful.
During this past year and three months, have you had any periods of a few months or longer where you felt completely like your usual, happy self?

Um, completely like my usual self? Well... let me think. There have definitely been some really nice, calm weeks in there. Times when my mood was actually pretty good, and I wasn't feeling all revved up or, you know, going without sleep. So I was doing okay in that regard! 

But... um... I guess if I'm being completely honest—and I hesitate to even say this out loud, because I know it sounds a little silly and it's probably just stress from the office—but even during those good stretches, for a couple of weeks or more, I still had some... well, some quirks, I guess you could call them. 

Like, I'd swear I heard someone calling my name when no one was around. Or I'd get this really intense feeling that just ordinary, everyday comments from my coworkers were actually... like, secret, coded tests to see if I was doing my job right. 

I know that probably sounds a bit strange, I'm sorry. I really try not to let it bother me, and I always stay professional at work regardless. Does that... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

When you have these experiences of hearing your name or feeling like your coworkers are testing you, do they happen only when you are feeling at your absolute lowest, or do they happen even when your mood is relatively stable and you're feeling more like yourself?

Um, yes, I think... well, it's like I mentioned, they actually happen even when I'm feeling pretty stable. 

I know it sounds like something that would only happen when I'm really down, but honestly, there have been those nice, calm weeks where I wasn't feeling depressed, and I wasn't feeling all revved up or skipping sleep either. My mood was actually quite good! But... um... even during those times, for more than a couple of weeks, I would still hear my name being called out of nowhere. Or I'd still get that strong feeling that those normal, everyday comments from the team were actually coded tests about my performance. 

I really hope I'm explaining that clearly. It's a bit embarrassing to admit that it happens even when I'm feeling okay, but I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that what you were asking?
During this past year, have you ever felt so low for at least two weeks that you lost interest in almost everything, had very little energy, and struggled with your appetite or sleep?

Um, oh, a full two weeks of feeling that low? Well, I don't... I really don't think so. I mean, everyone has a bad day here and there, right? Especially when things get busy at the office or when I'm trying to help out my family. 

But losing interest in everything and having no energy for weeks on end? No, I always make sure to keep up with my responsibilities. I wouldn't let myself just stop doing things. My appetite and sleep have been pretty normal for the most part, too. I try to take good care of myself so I can be there for the people who need me. 

I really try to stay positive, you know? I hope that's a good thing. Does that answer your question okay?

When you have these feelings that your coworkers are testing you, do you ever find yourself becoming convinced that they are actually conspiring against you or monitoring you in a way that you feel you need to protect yourself from?

Um, conspiring against me? Oh, no, no, I wouldn't use a strong word like that. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm paranoid or anything like that, because I know my coworkers are good people. 

It's just... well, sometimes I get a little caught up in things. Even on weeks when I'm not feeling especially energized or anything, I can get... I guess you could say convinced that little things, like calendar glitches or certain comments made during staff meetings, are actually signs. Like maybe someone is checking to see if I can still handle my job with everything going on with my family situation. 

I know it sounds a bit much, and I really try to just brush it off. But sometimes it's hard for me to let that feeling go, even when someone points out a perfectly simple, logical explanation for the glitch or the comment. I just... I get stuck on the idea that it's a test. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too crazy. I really do try to stay professional and keep everything running smoothly at the office. Is it okay that I feel that way sometimes?

When you have these thoughts that your coworkers are testing you, do you ever find yourself completely convinced that it is true, to the point where you feel you cannot be persuaded otherwise, even when presented with evidence that it isn't happening?

Um, well... I guess I sort of just mentioned that, but I can try to explain it a little better if that helps? I really don't want to sound like I'm completely unreasonable or, you know, totally out of touch with reality. I know how important it is to be professional in my role.

But, um... yes, I suppose there are times when I do get pretty convinced. Like I said, even on those normal weeks when I'm not feeling particularly energized or anything, if there's a calendar glitch or a specific comment in a staff meeting, I get this... this very strong feeling that it's a sign. That someone is testing to see if my family situation is affecting my work. 

And, um, even if someone explains it to me—like, "Oh, the server was just down," or "They didn't mean it that way"—it's... it's really hard for me to just let it go. I want to believe them, I really do, but I still feel stuck on the idea that it was a test. 

I try my best not to let it show or cause a problem at work, though. I really hope that makes sense. Am I explaining that the way you need me to?

Aside from the experiences you've mentioned, have you ever felt that your thoughts or speech were jumbled, or that you were having trouble organizing your daily life or taking care of yourself in a way that people around you noticed?

Oh, no, definitely not. I mean, my job as an executive assistant requires me to be extremely organized and clear-headed. If my thoughts were jumbled or if I couldn't communicate properly, I wouldn't be able to support my team the way I do. 

I always make sure I'm put together, you know? I dress professionally, keep my apartment tidy, and manage my schedule really carefully. I would be so embarrassed if someone thought I wasn't taking care of myself or couldn't handle my daily life. I really pride myself on being reliable and put together. 

I hope that's the right kind of answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything, because I really am doing my best to keep everything on track.
Besides hearing your name being called, have you ever seen things that other people couldn't see, or noticed visual patterns or movements that you later realized weren't actually there?

Um, seeing things? Oh, no, no, I've never seen anything like that. I wouldn't want you to think I'm seeing visions or anything, that sounds... well, that sounds very serious, and I definitely don't have that problem. My vision is perfectly fine. 

But, um, since you mentioned hearing my name... I guess I should probably mention that sometimes, it's a little more than just my name. I hope it doesn't sound too strange, because it really only happens when I'm completely alone. Like, if I'm sitting at my desk after everyone has gone to lunch, or maybe when I'm driving back from an appointment. 

I'll hear my name, or sometimes just a really quick little comment. Something work-related, usually, like... like, "fix the schedule." And it sounds so clear, honestly, just as clear as if one of the executives is standing right next to me. But then I turn around, and... well, there's nobody there. 

I always just assume it's my brain working overtime because I'm so focused on making sure everything is perfect for the team. It's just stress, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm losing my grip. I'm still doing a great job at work, I promise. Is it normal to have something like that happen when you're under a lot of pressure?

Have you ever had a period of at least one month where you experienced other symptoms, such as disorganized speech, extremely strange behavior, or a significant loss of motivation that made it difficult for you to function in your daily life?

Oh, goodness, no. Never a whole month, or... or even a few days of anything like that. 

Like I was mentioning before about my job, I just couldn't get away with that. If I started speaking in a disorganized way or acting strangely, the executives would notice right away, and I would be absolutely mortified. I try so hard to maintain a really professional image, and I would never want anyone to think I was behaving bizarrely. 

And as for losing motivation... well, I always push myself to keep going, even if I'm tired or stressed out. I really pride myself on my work ethic and keeping my life in order. I've never just stopped functioning or let my daily life fall apart. I always make sure I'm contributing and doing what's expected of me.

I really hope I'm giving you the right information? I just want to assure you that I'm very capable of handling my responsibilities, and I'm honestly doing my best to be a good, reliable person. Is that the kind of answer you were looking for?
